q: Children Education Allowance is admissible in respect of the third child of a railway servant where:

options.A: The first two children of the railway servant are studying in a hostel away from his headquarters
options.B: The railway servant has been transferred in public interest after the birth of the third child
options.C: The second confinement of the mother results in the birth of twins or multiple children, taking the number of children beyond two
options.D: The third child is a differently abled child

e: Children Education Allowance is normally restricted to two children, but the ceiling does not apply where the number exceeds two because the second confinement results in the birth of twins or multiple children, so the third child is covered in that case.

q: Where a public authority fails to supply the information sought under the Right to Information Act, 2005 within the time limit prescribed for the purpose, the information shall thereafter be supplied to the applicant:

options.A: On payment of twice the prescribed fee
options.B: Free of charge
options.C: Only after the orders of the First Appellate Authority are obtained
options.D: On payment of the cost of the information as assessed by the public authority

e: Where the public authority fails to furnish the information within the time limit prescribed under the RTI Act, the information must thereafter be supplied to the applicant free of charge.

q: The monthly subscription payable by a Group 'B' railway servant under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is:

options.B: Rs 30
options.C: Rs 120
options.D: Rs 80

e: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the monthly subscription is graded by group; for a Group B railway servant it is Rs 60, a part going to the insurance fund and the rest to the savings fund.

q: A railway servant who is appointed, promoted or granted a financial upgradation during the period from 2nd July to 1st January (both days inclusive) will draw his annual increment on:

options.B: The anniversary of the date of his appointment or promotion
options.C: 1st April
options.D: 1st July

e: Under the two-increment-date system, a servant appointed, promoted or granted financial upgradation during the period from 2nd July to 1st January draws his annual increment on 1st July.

q: An application seeking information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 may be made by the applicant in:

options.B: Hindi only
options.C: English or Hindi or in the official language of the area in which the application is made
options.D: The language in which the information is held by the public authority

e: Section 6 of the RTI Act permits an application to be made in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area in which the application is made.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the total amount of deductions which may be made from the wages of an employed person in any wage period shall not ordinarily exceed:

options.B: 50 per cent of the wages, and 75 per cent where any part of the deductions is made towards payments to co-operative societies
options.C: 60 per cent of the wages
options.D: 75 per cent of the wages in all cases

e: The Payment of Wages Act caps total deductions at 50 per cent of wages in a wage period, the limit rising to 75 per cent where any part of the deductions is towards payments to co-operative societies.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised class of pension under the pension rules applicable to railway servants?

options.B: Compensation pension
options.C: Anticipatory pension
options.D: Invalid pension

e: The recognised classes of pension include superannuation, retiring, invalid and compensation pension; "anticipatory pension" is not a class recognised under the pension rules applicable to railway servants.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a Welfare Officer is required to be appointed in every factory wherein the number of workers ordinarily employed is:

options.B: One hundred or more
options.C: Two hundred and fifty or more
options.D: One thousand or more

e: Under the Factories Act, a Welfare Officer is required to be appointed in every factory wherein 500 or more workers are ordinarily employed.

q: Non-Practising Allowance admissible to railway medical officers under the 7th CPC dispensation is payable at the rate of:

options.B: 15 per cent of basic pay
options.C: 30 per cent of basic pay
options.D: 20 per cent of basic pay

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Non-Practising Allowance admissible to railway medical officers, in lieu of private practice, is payable at 20 per cent of basic pay.

q: Recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group 'D') posts on the Railways is conducted through:

options.B: The Railway Recruitment Cells of the zonal railways
options.C: The Union Public Service Commission
options.D: The Staff Selection Commission

e: Recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group D) posts on the Railways is conducted through the Railway Recruitment Cells of the zonal railways, and not by the Railway Recruitment Boards or the UPSC.

q: The Unified Pension Scheme, introduced as an option for railway servants covered under the National Pension System, came into effect from:

options.B: 1st January, 2025
options.C: 24th January, 2025
options.D: 1st April, 2025

e: The Unified Pension Scheme, introduced as an option for railway servants covered under the National Pension System, came into effect from 1st April, 2025.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a railway servant for participating in a mountaineering expedition approved by the Indian Mountaineering Foundation can be granted up to:

options.B: 10 days in a calendar year
options.C: 15 days in a calendar year
options.D: 45 days in a calendar year

e: Special Casual Leave for participating in a mountaineering expedition approved by the Indian Mountaineering Foundation can be granted up to a maximum of 30 days in a calendar year.

q: The leave account of a non-gazetted railway servant is maintained:

options.A: By the Accounts Office which checks his pay bills
options.B: By the pension section of the zonal railway headquarters
options.C: In the prescribed form, along with his Service Book, by the office in which he is serving
options.D: By the office of the General Manager of the zonal railway

e: The leave account of a non-gazetted railway servant is maintained in the prescribed form, along with his Service Book, by the office in which he is serving.

q: Where a railway pensioner fails to draw his pension for a continuous period of more than one year, the correct position is that the pension:

options.A: Is forfeited permanently to the Government
options.B: Ceases to be payable and can be resumed only with the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Continues to accumulate and is paid in full, on demand, at any time thereafter
options.D: Is transferred to the credit of the Staff Benefit Fund

e: Pension not drawn for a continuous period of more than one year ceases to be payable, and it can be resumed only with the sanction of the competent authority.

q: Which of the following advances admissible to railway servants stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation?

options.B: House Building Advance
options.C: Personal Computer Advance
options.D: Advance in connection with Leave Travel Concession

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Festival Advance stands abolished, while House Building Advance, Personal Computer Advance and the advance in connection with LTC continue to be admissible.

q: Special Disability Leave is admissible to a railway servant when he is:

options.A: Suffering from any illness, whether or not it is connected with the discharge of his official duties
options.B: Disabled by injury accidentally incurred in, or in consequence of, the due execution of his official duties, or by illness incurred in the course of his official duty
options.C: Required to undergo a surgical operation in a railway hospital
options.D: Absent from duty for a period exceeding 120 days on medical grounds

e: Special Disability Leave is admissible only when the railway servant is disabled by injury accidentally incurred in, or in consequence of, the due execution of his official duties, or by illness incurred in the course of his official duty.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 29,600 in Level 4 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 5. One increment is first granted to him in Level 4, taking his pay to the next cell of Rs 30,500, and his pay is then fixed in Level 5 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 5 will be:
e: Working: 29,600 plus one increment in Level 4 gives 30,500; pay in Level 5 is fixed at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount, i.e. Rs 31,000.

q: A 'permanent post' under the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants means:

options.A: A post carrying a definite rate of pay sanctioned without limit of time
options.B: A post sanctioned for a limited period of one year at a time
options.C: A post held by a railway servant on confirmation
options.D: A post whose pay is charged to the revenue budget of the Railways

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, a permanent post means a post carrying a definite rate of pay sanctioned without limit of time, as against a temporary post sanctioned for a limited period.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 66,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Working: pension on full qualifying service is 50 per cent of average emoluments: 50 per cent of Rs 66,000 = Rs 33,000 per month.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A subscriber may enhance the amount of his subscription to the Provident Fund up to twice in the course of a financial year.
2. A subscriber may reduce the amount of his subscription to the Provident Fund once in the course of a financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a subscriber may enhance his Provident Fund subscription up to twice, and reduce it once, in the course of a financial year, within the prescribed limits.

q: Travelling Allowance on tour is NOT admissible to a railway servant for a journey to a place which is within the following distance from his headquarters or duty point:

options.B: 8 kilometres
options.C: 10 kilometres
options.D: 16 kilometres

e: Travelling Allowance on tour is not admissible for a journey to a place within 8 kilometres of the headquarters or duty point of the railway servant.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 24 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 68,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him will be:
e: Working: retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 17,000 x 48 periods (24 years) = Rs 8,16,000.

q: Where an application seeking information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is made to the Assistant Public Information Officer, the information is required to be furnished within:

options.A: 30 days of the receipt of the application
options.B: 45 days of the receipt of the application
options.C: 40 days of the receipt of the application
options.D: 35 days of the receipt of the application

e: An application received through the Assistant Public Information Officer carries five extra days over the normal period, so the information is required to be furnished within 35 days of receipt of the application.

q: Rule 20 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from:

options.A: Bringing or attempting to bring any political or other influence to bear upon any superior authority to further his interests in respect of matters pertaining to his service
options.B: Submitting a representation to his superior officer in respect of a service matter
options.C: Becoming a member of a recognised trade union of railway servants
options.D: Approaching the grievance redressal machinery of the Railways

e: Rule 20 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from bringing or attempting to bring any political or other influence to bear upon a superior authority to further his interests in service matters.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 35,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Working: monthly pension commuted = 40 per cent of Rs 35,000 = Rs 14,000; commuted value = 14,000 x 12 x 8.194 = Rs 13,76,592.

q: Special Disability Leave granted to a railway servant is:

options.A: Debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Debited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account
options.C: Not debited to his leave account
options.D: Treated as Extra Ordinary Leave for the purpose of the leave account

e: Special Disability Leave is a special kind of leave granted for disability connected with duty and is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay or Leave on Half Average Pay account.

q: Where a railway servant is appointed to another post which does NOT involve the assumption of duties and responsibilities of greater importance than those of the post held by him, his pay in the new post is fixed:

options.A: At the minimum of the pay level of the new post
options.B: By granting him one increment in the new post in all cases
options.C: At the stage next below the pay drawn by him in the old post
options.D: At the stage equal to the pay drawn by him in the old post, and if there is no such stage, at the next higher stage

e: Where the new post does not involve duties of greater importance, pay is fixed at the stage equal to the pay drawn in the old post, and if there is no such stage, at the next higher stage.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 35,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house, the estimated cost of construction being Rs 60 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him will be:
e: Working: House Building Advance is limited to 139 times basic pay or the cost of the house, whichever is less: 139 x Rs 35,000 = Rs 48,65,000, which is less than the estimated cost of Rs 60 lakh.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the total amount of fine that may be imposed on an employed person in any one wage period shall not exceed:

options.A: 5 per cent of his wages for that wage period
options.B: 10 per cent of his wages for that wage period
options.C: 3 per cent of his wages for that wage period
options.D: 7.5 per cent of his wages for that wage period

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, the total amount of fine that may be imposed on an employed person in any one wage period shall not exceed 3 per cent of his wages for that wage period.

q: In regard to the period of suspension of a railway servant for the purpose of pension, the correct position is that the period:

options.A: Counts as qualifying service in all cases, irrespective of the orders passed on his reinstatement
options.B: Counts as qualifying service only where the competent authority directs that the period shall be treated as duty, or otherwise orders it to be counted
options.C: Never counts as qualifying service in any case
options.D: Counts as qualifying service to the extent of one-half of the period of suspension

e: The period of suspension counts as qualifying service for pension only where the competent authority directs that it shall be treated as duty, or otherwise orders it to be counted.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 88,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate will be:

options.B: Rs 26,400 per month
options.C: Rs 52,800 per month
options.D: Rs 88,000 per month

e: Enhanced family pension is payable at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn: 50 per cent of Rs 88,000 = Rs 44,000 per month, admissible for 7 years or until the deceased would have attained 67 years, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant who is sent on deputation to an ex-cadre post:

options.A: Acquires a right to permanent absorption in the ex-cadre post on completion of the deputation period
options.B: Can claim absorption in the ex-cadre post as a matter of right after five years of deputation
options.C: Is entitled to continue in the ex-cadre post indefinitely at his option
options.D: Acquires no right to claim permanent absorption in the ex-cadre post, the deputation being for a fixed tenure

e: A railway servant on deputation to an ex-cadre post holds it for a fixed tenure only and acquires no right to claim permanent absorption in that post.

q: The minimum age prescribed for appointment to a post in railway service is:

options.B: 21 years
options.C: 18 years
options.D: 25 years

e: The minimum age prescribed for appointment to a post in railway service is 18 years.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 150 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 90,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Working: cash equivalent = (pay + DA) divided by 30 x days of leave: (90,000 + 45,000) / 30 x 150 = Rs 4,500 x 150 = Rs 6,75,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant may, without the previous sanction of the Government, undertake honorary work of a social or charitable nature.
2. A railway servant may, while on leave, take up private employment without obtaining the sanction of the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: honorary work of a social or charitable nature may be undertaken without previous sanction. Statement 2 is incorrect: private employment while on leave requires the sanction of the competent authority. Hence 1 only.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the periods of work of an adult worker in a factory shall be so arranged that, including his intervals for rest, they shall not spread over more than the following period in any day:

options.B: 10 1/2 hours
options.C: 12 hours
options.D: 8 1/2 hours

e: Under the Factories Act, the periods of work of an adult worker, including his intervals for rest, shall not spread over more than 10 1/2 hours in any day.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 62,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Working: Government contribution to NPS Tier-I is 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 14 per cent of (62,000 + 31,000) = 14 per cent of Rs 93,000 = Rs 13,020.

q: A 'tenure post' under the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants means:

options.A: A permanent post which an individual railway servant may not ordinarily hold for more than a limited period
options.B: A post held by a railway servant during his period of probation
options.C: A temporary post sanctioned for a work of short duration
options.D: A post from which a railway servant can be removed at any time without notice

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, a tenure post means a permanent post which an individual railway servant may not ordinarily hold for more than a limited period.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, whenever the Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants rises by 50 per cent, the rates of Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy are increased by:

options.B: 50 per cent
options.C: There is no increase on this account
options.D: 25 per cent

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, whenever Dearness Allowance rises by 50 per cent, the rates of Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy are increased by 25 per cent.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 4 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 48,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:
e: Working: death gratuity for qualifying service of one year or more but less than five years is six times the emoluments: 6 x Rs 48,000 = Rs 2,88,000.

q: A railway servant appointed to officiate in a higher post for a period of less than 14 days is entitled to:

options.A: Only the pay of his substantive (lower) post, the benefit of fixation of pay in the higher post not being admissible for such a short period
options.B: The pay of the higher post for the entire period of officiation
options.C: An officiating allowance at the rate of 10 per cent of his substantive pay
options.D: Two advance increments in his substantive post

e: Officiating in a higher post for a period of less than 14 days does not earn the benefit of pay fixation in the higher post; only the pay of the substantive post is admissible for such a short period.

q: Where a railway servant disappears and his whereabouts are not known, his family becomes eligible for the grant of family pension and other retirement benefits, after lodging a report with the police and subject to the prescribed conditions, on the expiry of:

options.A: Six months from the date of his disappearance
options.B: Two years from the date of his disappearance
options.C: One year from the date of his disappearance
options.D: Seven years from the date of his disappearance

e: Where a railway servant disappears, his family becomes eligible for family pension and other retirement benefits, after lodging a police report and subject to the prescribed conditions, on the expiry of one year from the date of disappearance.

q: A railway pensioner whose basic pension is Rs 52,000 per month attains the age of 95 years. The additional quantum of pension admissible to him will be:

options.B: Rs 15,600 per month
options.C: Rs 20,800 per month
options.D: Rs 26,000 per month

e: The additional quantum of pension at the age of 95 years is 50 per cent of the basic pension: 50 per cent of Rs 52,000 = Rs 26,000 per month.

q: Where promotion to a grade is made on a non-selection basis, i.e., on the basis of seniority-cum-suitability, the inter-se seniority of the railway servants so promoted in the higher grade is determined by:

options.A: Their order of position in a merit list prepared by a selection board
options.B: Their inter-se seniority in the lower (feeder) grade
options.C: The dates on which they actually assume charge of the higher post
options.D: Their respective dates of birth

e: Where promotion is on a non-selection basis, i.e. seniority-cum-suitability, the promoted railway servants carry their inter-se seniority of the lower feeder grade into the higher grade.

q: The amount of insurance cover admissible to the family of a Group 'B' railway servant who dies while in service, under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, is:
e: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the insurance cover for a Group B railway servant, payable to his family on death while in service, is Rs 60,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation under the Unified Pension Scheme after rendering 27 years of qualifying service. The average of his basic pay drawn during the last 12 months is Rs 84,000 per month. The assured payout admissible to him will be:

options.B: Rs 50,400 per month
options.C: Rs 42,000 per month
options.D: Rs 84,000 per month

e: Working: under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout for 25 years or more of qualifying service is 50 per cent of the average basic pay of the last 12 months: 50 per cent of Rs 84,000 = Rs 42,000 per month.

q: A railway servant on tour is provided with free lodging only, the boarding being arranged and paid for by himself. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day will be:

options.B: 25 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.C: 75 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.D: 50 per cent of the Daily Allowance

e: Daily Allowance is regulated by the facilities provided free: where free lodging only is provided and boarding is arranged and paid for by the servant himself, DA is admissible at 50 per cent of the normal rate.

q: On his first appointment to railway service, a Group 'A' or Group 'B' railway servant is required to submit:

options.A: Only a declaration of the movable property held by him
options.B: A return of his assets and liabilities, in the prescribed form, showing the movable, immovable and valuable property held by him
options.C: A copy of his income tax return for the preceding year
options.D: No return of property of any kind

e: On first appointment, a Group A or Group B railway servant is required to submit a return of his assets and liabilities in the prescribed form, showing the movable, immovable and valuable property held by him.

q: A railway servant who is himself drawing pension is also the spouse of a deceased railway servant. In regard to the two pensions, the correct position is that he:

options.A: Can draw both his own pension and the family pension admissible in respect of his deceased spouse at the same time
options.B: Can draw only the higher of the two pensions
options.C: Can draw only his own pension, the family pension not being admissible to him
options.D: Must surrender his own pension in order to draw the family pension

e: A railway servant who is himself a pensioner can draw both his own pension and the family pension admissible in respect of his deceased spouse at the same time; one does not bar the other.

q: Where it is proposed to impose on a railway servant the penalty of withholding of increments of pay for a period exceeding three years, the penalty can be imposed:

options.A: Without holding any inquiry, as it is a minor penalty
options.B: After a summary inquiry by the controlling officer
options.C: Only after holding an inquiry in the manner prescribed for imposing a major penalty
options.D: Only with the prior approval of the Railway Board

e: Withholding of increments for a period exceeding three years affects pay and pension cumulatively, so the penalty can be imposed only after holding an inquiry in the manner prescribed for imposing a major penalty.

q: If a railway servant does not exercise his option for fixation of pay on promotion within the stipulated period of one month from the date of his promotion, his pay is fixed:

options.A: From the date of his next increment in the lower post in all cases
options.B: At the minimum of the higher level in all cases
options.C: Only from the date on which he submits the option in writing thereafter
options.D: In accordance with FR 22(I)(a)(1), that is, with effect from the date of his promotion

e: If the option for fixation of pay on promotion is not exercised within one month, pay is fixed in accordance with FR 22(I)(a)(1), that is, with effect from the date of promotion itself.

q: Where a subscriber to the National Pension System dies while in service, the nominee or legal heir of the subscriber is entitled to:

options.A: Withdraw only 40 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth, the balance being compulsorily utilised for purchase of an annuity
options.B: Withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth in the Tier-I account as a lump sum, the purchase of an annuity not being mandatory in the case of death of the subscriber
options.C: Withdraw only 25 per cent of the subscriber's own contribution
options.D: No withdrawal, as the accumulated pension wealth lapses to the Government

e: On the death of an NPS subscriber while in service, the nominee or legal heir may withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth in the Tier-I account as a lump sum; purchase of an annuity is not mandatory in the case of death.

q: The Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme differs from the erstwhile Assured Career Progression (ACP) scheme in that the financial upgradation under MACP is granted:

options.A: In the immediate next higher Level of the pay matrix, irrespective of the promotional hierarchy of the post
options.B: In the next higher grade in the promotional hierarchy of the post, as under the ACP scheme
options.C: Only twice in the entire service of a railway servant
options.D: Only on the recommendations of a Departmental Promotion Committee for a selection post

e: Under MACP, the financial upgradation is granted in the immediate next higher Level of the pay matrix, irrespective of the promotional hierarchy, whereas under ACP it followed the next higher grade in the promotional hierarchy.

q: The Travelling Allowance admissible to a railway servant on retirement, for the journey of himself and his family to his home town or other selected place of settlement, can be availed of within:

options.A: Three months from the date of his retirement
options.B: Six months from the date of his retirement
options.C: One year from the date of his retirement
options.D: Two years from the date of his retirement

e: Travelling Allowance on retirement, for the journey of the railway servant and his family to the home town or selected place of settlement, can be availed of within one year from the date of retirement.

q: A legal practitioner can be engaged by a charged railway servant as his defence assistant in a departmental inquiry where:

options.A: Legal practitioners can be engaged in every departmental inquiry as a matter of right
options.B: The charged railway servant has been placed under suspension
options.C: The inquiry relates to a minor penalty only
options.D: The Presenting Officer is a legal practitioner, or the disciplinary authority, having regard to the circumstances of the case, permits such engagement

e: A legal practitioner can be engaged as defence assistant only where the Presenting Officer is a legal practitioner, or the disciplinary authority, having regard to the circumstances of the case, permits such engagement.

q: The Right to Information Act, 2005 came into force on:

options.B: 12th October, 2005
options.C: 1st January, 2006
options.D: 26th January, 2006

e: The Right to Information Act, 2005 came into force on 12th October, 2005.

q: The application fee prescribed under the Right to Information Act, 2005 can be paid by an applicant:

options.A: By cash against proper receipt, or by demand draft, banker's cheque or Indian Postal Order drawn in favour of the Accounts Officer of the public authority
options.B: Only in cash at the office of the public authority
options.C: Only by a crossed cheque drawn in favour of the Central Public Information Officer
options.D: Only by money order addressed to the public authority

e: The application fee under the RTI Act can be paid by cash against proper receipt, or by demand draft, banker's cheque or Indian Postal Order drawn in favour of the Accounts Officer of the public authority.

q: A railway servant who is transferred from one seniority unit to another on administrative grounds, in public interest, is assigned seniority in the new unit:

options.A: At the bottom of the seniority list of the new unit, as in the case of a transfer on his own request
options.B: Above all the railway servants already borne in the new unit
options.C: With reference to the length of service rendered by him in the grade in the old unit, and not necessarily at the bottom of the seniority list
options.D: With reference to his date of birth, irrespective of his service in the grade

e: A transfer on administrative grounds in public interest is not treated like an own-request transfer; seniority in the new unit is assigned with reference to the length of service rendered in the grade in the old unit, and not necessarily at the bottom.

q: On the exit of a subscriber from the National Pension System, the annuity for providing pension to him is purchased from:

options.A: The Life Insurance Corporation of India only
options.B: An Annuity Service Provider empanelled by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
options.C: Any insurance company of the choice of the subscriber
options.D: The Accounts Office of the Railway in which he last served

e: On exit from the National Pension System, the annuity for providing pension is purchased from an Annuity Service Provider empanelled by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.

q: 'Personal pay' granted to a railway servant to save him from a loss of substantive pay is ordinarily:

options.A: Never absorbed in any subsequent increase of pay
options.B: Admissible only during the period of his probation
options.C: Counted as pay only for the purpose of Dearness Allowance
options.D: Absorbed in the subsequent increases of pay of the railway servant in the post

e: Personal pay granted to save a railway servant from a loss of substantive pay is ordinarily absorbed in the subsequent increases of pay in the post, so that it does not continue indefinitely.

q: Invalid pension is admissible to a railway servant who retires from service on being declared by the competent medical authority to be permanently incapacitated for further service:

options.A: Only if he has completed not less than 20 years of qualifying service
options.B: Even if he has not completed 10 years of qualifying service
options.C: Only if he has completed not less than 25 years of qualifying service
options.D: Only if the incapacity is directly attributable to his official duties

e: Invalid pension is admissible to a railway servant declared permanently incapacitated for further service by the competent medical authority, even if he has not completed 10 years of qualifying service.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Child Care Leave granted to a railway servant is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant.
2. Child Care Leave can be granted in a spell of less than five days.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: Child Care Leave is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant. Statement 2 is incorrect: CCL cannot be granted in a spell of less than five days. Hence 1 only.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 92,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Working: pension on full qualifying service is 50 per cent of average emoluments: 50 per cent of Rs 92,000 = Rs 46,000 per month.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Extra Ordinary Leave from a period of absence treated as 'dies non'?

options.A: Extra Ordinary Leave carries half leave salary, whereas no leave salary is payable for a period treated as dies non
options.B: Dies non is a recognised kind of leave, whereas Extra Ordinary Leave is not a recognised kind of leave
options.C: Both Extra Ordinary Leave and dies non can be granted only on production of a medical certificate
options.D: Extra Ordinary Leave is a recognised kind of leave granted by the competent authority when no other leave is admissible, whereas dies non is the treatment meted out to a period of absence which is neither duty nor leave

e: Extra Ordinary Leave is a recognised kind of leave, granted by the competent authority when no other leave is admissible, whereas dies non is the treatment of a period of absence which is neither duty nor leave.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 15 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 44,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him will be:
e: Working: retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 11,000 x 30 periods (15 years) = Rs 3,30,000.

q: Night Duty Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation is admissible only to a railway servant whose basic pay does not exceed:

options.B: Rs 60,000 per month
options.C: Rs 25,000 per month
options.D: There is no ceiling of basic pay for the admissibility of this allowance

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Night Duty Allowance is admissible only to a railway servant whose basic pay does not exceed Rs 43,600 per month.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 48,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate will be:

options.B: Rs 19,200 per month
options.C: Rs 9,600 per month
options.D: Rs 14,400 per month

e: Working: family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn: 30 per cent of Rs 48,000 = Rs 14,400 per month.

q: Rule 3-A of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant, in the discharge of his official duties, to:

options.A: Maintain absolute integrity and devotion to duty at all times
options.B: Submit a return of his assets and liabilities on his first appointment
options.C: Act with promptness and courtesy and not adopt dilatory tactics or wilfully cause delays in the disposal of the work assigned to him
options.D: Manage his private affairs so as to avoid habitual indebtedness

e: Rule 3-A of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant to act with promptness and courtesy and not to adopt dilatory tactics or wilfully cause delays in the disposal of the work assigned to him.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 17 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 42,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: For 11 years or more but less than 20 years of qualifying service, death gratuity is 20 times the emoluments: 20 x Rs 42,000 = Rs 8,40,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant appointed by direct recruitment, who is still on probation, may be discharged from service if his work or conduct is found to be unsatisfactory during the period of probation.
2. A railway servant promoted to a higher post, who fails to complete the period of probation in that post satisfactorily, may be reverted to the lower post held by him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a direct recruit on probation may be discharged if his work or conduct is unsatisfactory, and a promoted servant who fails to complete probation satisfactorily may be reverted to the lower post.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 120 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 72,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Working: cash equivalent = (pay + DA) divided by 30 x days of leave: (72,000 + 36,000) / 30 x 120 = Rs 3,600 x 120 = Rs 4,32,000.

q: For the purpose of House Rent Allowance, a city is classified as 'Y' class if its population is:

options.B: 25 lakh and above but below 50 lakh
options.C: 10 lakh and above but below 25 lakh
options.D: 5 lakh and above but below 50 lakh

e: For House Rent Allowance, a city with population of 5 lakh and above but below 50 lakh is classified as Y class; 50 lakh and above is X class and below 5 lakh is Z class.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 56,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate will be:

options.B: Rs 28,000 per month
options.C: Rs 22,400 per month
options.D: Rs 56,000 per month

e: Working: enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn: 50 per cent of Rs 56,000 = Rs 28,000 per month.

q: A complaint of sexual harassment made by a woman railway employee at the workplace is required to be enquired into by:

options.A: The Internal Complaints Committee constituted under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
options.B: The Inquiring Authority appointed under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.C: The Central Public Information Officer of the Railway
options.D: The Staff Council of the office in which she is working

e: A complaint of sexual harassment at the workplace is enquired into by the Internal Complaints Committee constituted under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 22 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 50,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family will be:
e: Working: for qualifying service of 20 years or more, death gratuity is half a month's emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 25,000 x 44 periods (22 years) = Rs 11,00,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is enabled by Article 16(4A) of the Constitution.
2. Reservation in promotion is admissible for Other Backward Classes also, on the same footing as for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is enabled by Article 16(4A) of the Constitution. Statement 2 is incorrect: reservation in promotion is not admissible for Other Backward Classes. Hence 1 only.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 21,700 in Level 3 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 4. One increment is first granted to him in Level 3, taking his pay to the next cell of Rs 22,400, and his pay is then fixed in Level 4 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 4 will be:
e: Working: 21,700 plus one increment in Level 3 gives 22,400; in Level 4 there is no cell equal to or just above that amount below the minimum of the level, so pay is fixed at the minimum of Level 4, i.e. Rs 25,500.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'compulsory retirement' from 'premature retirement' of a railway servant?

options.A: Compulsory retirement is ordered in public interest under the retirement rules, whereas premature retirement is a penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules
options.B: Compulsory retirement is a major penalty imposed after disciplinary proceedings, whereas premature retirement ordered in public interest under the relevant retirement rules is not a penalty
options.C: There is no distinction between compulsory retirement and premature retirement
options.D: Premature retirement carries no pensionary benefits, whereas compulsory retirement carries full pensionary benefits in all cases

e: Compulsory retirement is a major penalty imposed after disciplinary proceedings under the Discipline and Appeal Rules, whereas premature retirement ordered in public interest under the retirement rules is not a penalty.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 7 years of qualifying service and is not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 36,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, in lieu of pension, will be:
e: Working: service gratuity, payable in lieu of pension, is half a month's emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 18,000 x 14 periods (7 years) = Rs 2,52,000.

q: Under the Right to Information (Fee and Cost) Rules, for inspection of records by an applicant, the fee chargeable is:

options.A: Rs 10 for every hour of inspection
options.B: Rs 5 for every hour of inspection, including the first hour
options.C: No fee for the first hour of inspection and Rs 5 for each subsequent hour (or fraction thereof)
options.D: A flat fee of Rs 50, irrespective of the duration of the inspection

e: Under the Right to Information (Fee and Cost) Rules, no fee is charged for the first hour of inspection of records, and Rs 5 is charged for each subsequent hour or fraction thereof.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 25,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house, the estimated cost of construction being Rs 40 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him will be:
e: Working: House Building Advance is limited to 139 times basic pay or the cost of the house, whichever is less: 139 x Rs 25,000 = Rs 34,75,000, which is less than the cost of Rs 40 lakh.

q: Under Article 16(4B) of the Constitution, the unfilled vacancies of a year which were reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and are carried forward as backlog vacancies are:

options.A: Treated as part of the vacancies of the succeeding year for applying the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation
options.B: Treated as lapsed at the end of the year in which they arise
options.C: Converted into unreserved vacancies after the expiry of one year
options.D: Considered as a separate and distinct class of vacancies, which are not taken into account along with the vacancies of the succeeding year for applying the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation

e: Under Article 16(4B), unfilled reserved vacancies carried forward as backlog vacancies are considered as a separate and distinct class of vacancies, not taken into account with the vacancies of the succeeding year for applying the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 60,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Working: monthly pension commuted = 40 per cent of Rs 60,000 = Rs 24,000; commuted value = 24,000 x 12 x 8.194 = Rs 23,59,872.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the wages of an employed person shall be paid:

options.A: Only in cash, in current coin or currency notes
options.B: Only by a cheque drawn in favour of the employed person
options.C: In current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the amount in the bank account of the employed person
options.D: Only through the salary bill prepared by the Accounts Office

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, wages may be paid in current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the amount in the bank account of the employed person.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 66,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Working: the railway servant's own NPS contribution is 10 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 10 per cent of (66,000 + 33,000) = 10 per cent of Rs 99,000 = Rs 9,900.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'special pay' from 'personal pay' of a railway servant?

options.A: Special pay is granted to save a railway servant from a loss of substantive pay, whereas personal pay is granted in consideration of the arduous nature of the duties
options.B: Special pay is granted in consideration of the specially arduous nature of the duties or of a specific addition to the work or responsibility, whereas personal pay is granted to save a railway servant from a loss of substantive pay
options.C: Special pay is admissible only to gazetted railway servants, whereas personal pay is admissible only to non-gazetted railway servants
options.D: There is no distinction between special pay and personal pay

e: Special pay is granted in consideration of the specially arduous nature of the duties or a specific addition to the work or responsibility, whereas personal pay is granted to save a railway servant from a loss of substantive pay.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation under the Unified Pension Scheme after rendering 30 years of qualifying service. His last drawn basic pay is Rs 70,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The lump sum payment admissible to him, at the rate of one-tenth of his last drawn basic pay plus dearness allowance for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Working: lump sum is one-tenth of last drawn basic pay plus DA for each six-monthly period: Rs 10,500 x 60 periods (30 years) = Rs 6,30,000.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, where the number of persons employed in an establishment is less than one thousand, the wages for a wage period must be paid before the expiry of the:

options.A: Seventh day after the last day of the wage period
options.B: Tenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.C: Fifteenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.D: Last day of the wage period itself

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, where the number of persons employed in an establishment is less than one thousand, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period.

q: A railway servant who is appointed to hold 'current charge' of the duties of a higher post, in addition to his own duties, is entitled to:

options.A: The pay of the higher post for the period for which he holds current charge of that post
options.B: Additional Post Allowance at the prescribed rate for the period of current charge
options.C: An officiating allowance at the rate of 10 per cent of his substantive pay
options.D: Only the pay of his own post, no additional pay being admissible for holding current charge of a higher post

e: Holding current charge of the duties of a higher post is a temporary arrangement in addition to one's own duties; only the pay of his own post is admissible and no additional pay is payable for it.

q: A railway servant drawing last basic pay of Rs 45,000 per month is transferred in public interest to another station, involving a change of residence. The Composite Transfer Grant admissible to him will be:
e: Working: Composite Transfer Grant on transfer in public interest involving change of residence is 80 per cent of the last basic pay: 80 per cent of Rs 45,000 = Rs 36,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tier-I account under the National Pension System is the mandatory pension account of the subscriber, from which withdrawals before the prescribed age of exit are restricted.
2. The Tier-II account under the National Pension System is a voluntary savings account, from which the subscriber can withdraw his savings at any time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Tier-I account is the mandatory pension account with restricted withdrawals before the prescribed exit age, while the Tier-II account is a voluntary savings account from which savings can be withdrawn at any time.

q: A railway servant who is transferred from one station to another on a mutual basis, by exchange of postings with another railway servant, is entitled to Travelling Allowance and Composite Transfer Grant:

options.A: Not admissible, as a mutual transfer is treated as a transfer on the railway servant's own request
options.B: Admissible in full, as in the case of a transfer in public interest
options.C: Admissible at 50 per cent of the rates admissible on a transfer in public interest
options.D: Admissible only where both the railway servants have completed ten years of service

e: A mutual transfer is treated as a transfer on the railway servant's own request, so Travelling Allowance and Composite Transfer Grant, admissible on a transfer in public interest, are not admissible.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'service gratuity' from 'retirement gratuity' payable to a railway servant?

options.A: Service gratuity is payable in addition to pension, whereas retirement gratuity is payable in lieu of pension
options.B: Both service gratuity and retirement gratuity are payable at the same rate and on the same conditions
options.C: Service gratuity is payable only on the death of a railway servant in service, whereas retirement gratuity is payable only on superannuation
options.D: Service gratuity is paid in lieu of pension to a railway servant retiring with less than ten years of qualifying service, at the rate of half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, whereas retirement gratuity is paid in addition to pension, at the rate of one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, to a railway servant who has completed not less than five years of qualifying service

e: Service gratuity is paid in lieu of pension for service under ten years, at half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period; retirement gratuity is paid in addition to pension, at one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period, after five years or more of service.

q: Under Rule 5 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, where any member of the family of a railway servant takes part in politics, or in any movement or activity which is subversive, and the railway servant is unable to prevent him from doing so, the railway servant shall:

options.B: Make a report in that behalf to the Government
options.C: Merely inform his immediate superior officer verbally about it
options.D: Take no action, as the conduct of his family members does not concern him

e: Under Rule 5 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, where a family member takes part in politics or a subversive movement and the railway servant is unable to prevent him, he shall make a report in that behalf to the Government.

q: A house or flat purchased or constructed by a railway servant with the help of House Building Advance granted to him is required to be:

options.A: Registered in the name of the Railway Administration
options.B: Insured by the railway servant against all risks at his own cost in every case
options.C: Mortgaged to the Government as security for the repayment of the advance
options.D: Sold only with the prior permission of the Accounts Office

e: A house or flat purchased or constructed with the help of House Building Advance is required to be mortgaged to the Government as security for the repayment of the advance.

q: For the purpose of reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in direct recruitment, a candidate is treated as belonging to the Economically Weaker Section where the gross annual income of his family from all sources is below:

options.B: Rs 6 lakh
options.C: Rs 10 lakh
options.D: Rs 12 lakh

e: For reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in direct recruitment, a candidate belongs to the EWS where the gross annual income of his family from all sources is below Rs 8 lakh.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'deputation' from 'foreign service' of a railway servant?

options.A: On deputation the railway servant receives his pay from a source other than the revenues of the Government, whereas on foreign service he receives his pay from the revenues of the Government
options.B: Foreign service can be rendered only in a foreign country, whereas deputation can be availed of only within India
options.C: There is no distinction between deputation and foreign service
options.D: On deputation the railway servant is posted to an ex-cadre post for a fixed tenure while retaining his lien in his parent cadre, whereas on foreign service he renders service in which he receives his pay, with the sanction of the Government, from a source other than the revenues of the Government or of the Railways

e: On deputation, the servant holds an ex-cadre post for a fixed tenure, retaining lien in the parent cadre; on foreign service, he receives his pay, with Government sanction, from a source other than Government or Railway revenues.

q: The Warm Clothing Advance, which was admissible to railway servants posted at hill stations, has been, under the 7th CPC dispensation:

options.A: Enhanced to twice the amount admissible earlier
options.B: Abolished
options.C: Converted into an interest-bearing advance
options.D: Merged with the House Building Advance

e: The Warm Clothing Advance, earlier admissible to railway servants posted at hill stations, stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation.

q: For the purpose of grant of family pension, the 'family' of a deceased railway servant includes:

options.A: A married son of the deceased railway servant who has attained the age of 30 years
options.B: A brother of the deceased railway servant, whether or not he was dependent on him
options.C: A son-in-law of the deceased railway servant
options.D: A legally adopted son of the deceased railway servant

e: For the grant of family pension, the family of a deceased railway servant includes a legally adopted son; married adult sons, brothers and sons-in-law are not included as such.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dearness Relief is admissible to family pensioners as well as to pensioners.
2. Dearness Relief is calculated on the basic pension or family pension, including the additional quantum admissible on attaining the age of 80 years and above.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Dearness Relief is admissible to family pensioners as well as pensioners, and it is calculated on the basic pension or family pension, including the additional quantum admissible on attaining the age of 80 years and above.
